text:
sam: FYI customer reported backend target becoming UNHEALTHY for NLB after a cert rotation earlier today. They see app responses in the pod but target group shows failed TLS probe :confused:
priya: can you paste the health check config (protocol/path/port) and whether it's IP or instance target?
sam: they used HTTPS /health on 443, target type = ip (k8s NodePort -> host network -> envoy). Health check config: Protocol=HTTPS, Port=443, path=/health, interval=10s, timeout=5s, healthy_threshold=3
chen: NLB HTTPS checks do TCP+TLS handshake then GET with Host? IIRC NLB health checks don't set SNI or Host header for TLS probe — that bites when Envoy is doing mTLS or SNI-based routing.
sam: customer confirmed Envoy config routes by SNI and expects client SNI = service.internal. Health checks were failing with TLS handshake alert.
priya: can you repro from a bastion inside the same subnet? Try curl and openssl s_client to see SNI behavior.
sam: did that from their bastion (10.10.5.12) — results:
```
$ curl -v --resolve service.internal:443:10.0.2.5 https://service.internal/health
* Connected to 10.0.2.5 (10.0.2.5) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...
* server certificate verification OK
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: service.internal
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
But tcpdump from the pod side during a failing probe showed ClientHello without SNI.
chen: can you paste the tcpdump/tshark summary?
sam: captured client hello summary (edited):
```
ClientHello, no SNI, cipher TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
```
We also saw handshake aborts with Alert(40) on the envoy logs.
priya: that matches NLB behavior — depending on health check type, the probe may not include SNI or Host header. If Envoy requires SNI, the handshake will fail -> UNHEALTHY.
chen: quick mitigation options: 1) switch NLB health check to TCP (port 443) so only TCP check — but that won't validate HTTP path; 2) use HTTP health checks via ALB in front of Envoy so Host header is present; 3) update Envoy to accept connections without SNI for the health-check listener (allow fallback certificate or match by IP).
sam: customer is hesitant to change Envoy. They asked if we can make NLB include SNI — AWS NLB does not send SNI on TCP/TLS health checks. ALB does HTTP/HTTPS checks and will send Host header for HTTPS (but might still not include SNI in the same way).
priya: another angle — is there an egress allowlist or firewall that rewrites or terminates TLS? Could be a proxy between NLB and pod that strips SNI. Any middlebox?
sam: they use on-prem firewall on the path from NLB nodes to backend (private VPC peering + firewall). They had an egress allowlist that only allowed specific destination IPs and also an inline TLS terminator for inspection. That box was updated earlier today coincident with cert rotation.
chen: that would explain intermittent behavior — when inspection is enabled it may terminate TLS and re-initiate without SNI. Can you get tcpdump on the backend when failing to confirm whether ClientHello is coming from NLB nodes or from the proxy IP?
sam: we did. client ip = 10.255.0.14 (NLB node) for some attempts, and 10.200.3.9 (firewall-proxy) for others. The firewall was doing TLS break-and-inspect and reissuing handshake without SNI.
priya: ok root cause: mix of direct NLB node checks and proxied checks causing missing SNI. Recommended fix: update Envoy to accept non-SNI connections on health check listener OR move to an ALB HTTP(S) health check that includes Host header; or adjust firewall to preserve SNI or avoid TLS inspection for health-check paths.
sam: customer will try config change: add a listener in Envoy accepting ANY SNI for /health on 127.0.0.1:someport and change k8s readiness to that port, then update service mapping so NLB probes hit that port. Also they will open a ticket with their firewall vendor to preserve SNI.
chen: action items: @sam - collect full tcpdump pcap and envoy logs and attach to support ticket. @priay - document recommended patterns in KB (NLB vs ALB vs Envoy SNI) so we can point future customers.
sam: support-bot: created ticket SI-98721 for this escalation and attached pcap/logs :white_check_mark:
support-bot: Ticket SI-98721 created and linked to internal case 2026-03-17-ACME.
priya: note for KB: "If backend requires SNI for routing, prefer ALB HTTPS checks or ensure a health-check listener on backend that doesn’t require SNI. NLB health probes can omit SNI. Also watch for middleboxes doing TLS inspection that may strip SNI."
chen: closing loop — customer applied temporary Envoy change and targets turned healthy after ~30s. They'll follow up with firewall team for a permanent fix. :thumbsup:
sam: closing thread, will add notes to case.
